verdict.rationale: Baseten's Model APIs documentation states that prompt tokens reused from a cached prefix are served from the KV cache at a discounted rate. Caching is automatic and needs no request flags, and requests sharing a session ID are routed to the same replica so the prefix is more likely to stay cached, which directly delivers the cost reduction on repeated context. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of latency reduction from cache hits (the docs cover cost only), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ml-engineer, I can benefit from prompt/prefix caching that reduces latency or cost on repeated context

citations.quote: Cached input tokens are prompt tokens served from the KV cache at a discounted rate. Caching is automatic and requires no request flags.
Baseten serves prompt tokens from the KV cache at a discounted rate when a request reuses a cached prefix.
Baseten routes requests with the same session ID to the same replica, where the shared prompt prefix is more likely to remain in the KV cache.
